key_insight: LCGuard enables safe latent communication by filtering and sanitizing transformer KV cache exchanges so agents keep coordination benefits without leaking contextual or sensitive information.
problem_solved: Prevents unintended disclosure of input context, intermediate reasoning, and agent-specific data when multi-agent LLMs share latent (KV) representations for coordination.
method: Learned latent filter that inspects KV caches and distinguishes task-relevant signals from sensitive/contextual content.
Sanitization mechanisms (masking, selective gating, or controlled perturbation) applied to KV entries to remove or obfuscate private information while preserving utility.
Optimization and evaluation under a utility–privacy tradeoff (e.g., adversarial training or regularizers) to retain coordination performance while limiting leakage.
impact: Allows practitioners to deploy efficient, KV-based latent communication in multi-agent systems with reduced privacy and leakage risks, enabling safer collaboration and regulatory compliance without major performance loss.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: agents → KV cache exchange → LCGuard filter → sanitized KV → coordinated output (before vs after highlighting removed sensitive content)
Bar or line chart: coordination performance vs. privacy leakage for baseline latent sharing and LCGuard (showing maintained utility with reduced leakage)
Heatmap or attention overlay on KV matrix showing which entries are preserved vs. masked by LCGuard
Icon set: LLM agents, shield (privacy), lock (access control), and speed/performance gauge
paper_title: LCGuard: Latent Communication Guard for Safe KV Sharing in Multi-Agent Systems
paper_authors: Sadia Asif, Mohammad Mohammadi Amiri, Momin Abbas, Prasanna Sattigeri, Karthikeyan Natesan Ramamurthy
